use_when: visual direction is open
one polished answer would anchor selection
entries.counterexample: A precisely specified local component does not need a direction tournament.
entries.observable_test: Directions differ in structure or interaction, not only palette, and share equal fidelity.
entries.claim_ceiling: Empirical support for breadth-first exploration; not proof that every three-option set improves quality.
entries.payload: Before polished implementation, compare equal-fidelity alternatives that differ structurally. Delay high-fidelity commitment until the user or a fresh selector can compare viable worlds.

source.title: Rethinking the UI of Generative UI

use_when: recent unrelated outputs share visual fingerprints
category default is predictable
avoid_when: shared brand or design-system authority explains the similarity
entries.counterexample: A multi-surface product should intentionally reuse its established visual world.
entries.observable_test: The selected direction can explain every major commitment through product mechanism, audience scene, platform authority, or explicit preference.
entries.payload: Name the category default, the model's recent cross-task prior, and the reflex anti-default. Treat all three as spent unless the brief earns one. Re-derive at least two axes when unrelated work repeats the same fingerprint without shared authority.

use_when: intent is difficult to articulate
requirements interact hierarchically
avoid_when: the source design already specifies the target exactly
entries.counterexample: A tiny literal implementation task may be clearer without another representation.
entries.observable_test: A reviewer can trace selected structure and interaction to explicit product semantics.
entries.claim_ceiling: Comparative-study evidence for control and interpretability, not universal outcome superiority.
entries.payload: Use a compact semantic representation between product intent and implementation. Preserve facts, decisions, hypotheses, defaults, and delegated choices as different states.

source.title: Bridging Gulfs in UI Generation through Semantic Guidance

use_when: visual preference is consequential
reviewers disagree
avoid_when: a normative or product-truth question is being decided
entries.counterexample: Accessibility conformance is not a personal preference vote.
entries.observable_test: Selections are recorded with rationale, confidence, scope, and non-generalization boundaries.
entries.claim_ceiling: Preference-model evidence; not a universal taste oracle.
entries.payload: Use sparse pairwise comparisons for consequential visual choices. Keep preference evidence project-local and scoped; do not convert one selection into a global style rule.

source.title: Efficient Personalization of Generative User Interfaces

use_when: one or two elements deserve amplified attention
competing attention exists
avoid_when: all compared objects are genuinely equal peers
entries.counterexample: A comparison matrix may intentionally give peer options equal exposure.
entries.observable_test: After five seconds, users identify the intended primary element and next action or decision.
entries.claim_ceiling: Conditional first-party empirical evidence for expressive hierarchy.
entries.payload: Declare primary, supporting, and quiet content. Amplify at most one or two elements; expression cannot compensate for an unfamiliar or broken interaction paradigm.

use_when: multiple local decisions must read as one authored system
avoid_when: a local extension inherits an established system unchanged
entries.counterexample: A deliberate exception may break one commitment when the product need is explicit.
entries.observable_test: Composition, type, color/material, shape/depth, motion, copy, and states reinforce the same thesis.
entries.payload: Freeze project-specific coherence commitments after direction selection. Commitments are not universal dials; each must cite product mechanism, audience scene, platform authority, explicit preference, or established authority.

use_when: a pattern resembles an AI default or checklist violation
avoid_when: direct evidence already establishes a normative failure
entries.counterexample: Cards, serif type, translucency, dense data, and conventional controls may be correct in context.
entries.observable_test: Every proposed edit names observed harm, a valid exception, why it does not control, and expected improvement.
entries.claim_ceiling: Evaluation safeguard inferred from false-positive and design-theater evidence.
entries.payload: Do not repair a pattern because it resembles an AI tell. Require observable harm, a valid counterexample, and a predicted user-visible improvement before changing it.

use_when: layout crosses materially different widths or postures
entries.counterexample: A fixed print artifact may preserve one composition.
entries.observable_test: At 320–375 px, priority, meaning, controls, and state remain usable without impairing overflow.
entries.claim_ceiling: Official platform practice and acceptance-test guidance.
entries.payload: Transform composition across widths rather than shrinking desktop structure. Preserve the current decision and intervention controls; collapse or defer supporting history and metrics when necessary.

use_when: interactive web controls exist
entries.counterexample: A purely decorative element is not an interactive target.
entries.observable_test: Keyboard focus is visible and not entirely obscured; pointer targets and dragging alternatives meet applicable WCAG 2.2 criteria.
entries.claim_ceiling: Normative WCAG 2.2 requirements only where applicable.
entries.payload: Verify focus visibility and non-obscuration, keyboard paths, target geometry, pointer cancellation, and non-drag alternatives where dragging implements functionality. Record not-applicable cases explicitly.

use_when: the artifact displays computed totals, contrast, size, status, or readiness
avoid_when: no computed or asserted values are shown
entries.counterexample: A static label copied from authoritative source content need not be recomputed.
entries.observable_test: Displayed values are derived from the actual current records or assets and fail when those inputs change.
entries.claim_ceiling: Project hardening heuristic from repeated Authorial 11.1 repairs.
entries.payload: Derive displayed totals, status, contrast, size, and preflight claims from current source records or assets. Hard-coded pass text is prohibited.

use_when: records can be added, removed, undone, exported, or named
entries.counterexample: A fixed read-only list can use source-provided stable IDs directly.
entries.observable_test: Add-add-remove-add and undo sequences preserve unique IDs, filenames, counts, previews, and manifest consistency.
entries.claim_ceiling: Project hardening heuristic from observed identity-production failure.
entries.payload: Use stable unique records as the single source for IDs, filenames, rendered items, counts, status, and manifests. Independent counters are prohibited.

use_when: required states or evidence captures are declared
entries.counterexample: An alternate local entry is acceptable when the acceptance contract tests the end state rather than the transition.
entries.observable_test: Every required state has a real pointer, keyboard, programmatic, or approved alternate-entry path and visible result.
entries.claim_ceiling: Project hardening heuristic from repeated evidence-state failures.
entries.payload: Bind every required state to an executable entry path and visible result before build freeze. A declared but unreachable state is missing, not unverified success.

use_when: AI proposes or performs consequential actions
avoid_when: AI only generates non-consequential static content
entries.counterexample: A low-stakes suggestion may use a quiet explanation layer rather than a persistent control panel.
entries.observable_test: Users can state capability limits, current lifecycle state, consequence before execution, and available correction or recovery.
entries.claim_ceiling: Peer-reviewed and mature-practice support for calibrated control and explanation.
entries.payload: Separate capability, reliability, and explanation. Expose edit, correct, dismiss, approve, cancel, retry, undo, and recovery according to consequence. Keep the current user decision ahead of trace history.

use_when: authored motion or micro-interaction is being considered
avoid_when: motion does not improve feedback, continuity, explanation, or state
entries.counterexample: Frequent keyboard actions are often better without authored motion.
entries.observable_test: The motion's purpose, frequency, origin, interruptibility, and reduced variant can be demonstrated.
entries.claim_ceiling: Practitioner craft guidance, not universal timing law.
entries.payload: Decide whether to animate from frequency and purpose. Favor immediate feedback, origin-aware and interruptible behavior, touch safety, and reduced-motion alternatives. No motion is a valid verdict.

use_when: the design makes claims about implemented behavior or rationale
entries.counterexample: A clearly labeled future recommendation is not an implementation claim.
entries.observable_test: Each material claim maps to an exact artifact region, state, and proof method.
entries.claim_ceiling: Benchmark evidence that rationale frequently exceeds implementation.
entries.payload: Treat design rationale as a hypothesis. Material claims require an implementation locus, observable state, and proof against the exact artifact version.

use_when: the product owns a payment or checkout flow
avoid_when: a third-party hosted flow owns data entry and states
entries.counterexample: A redirect-only integration should not invent fields it does not own.
entries.observable_test: Owned method, entry, validation, processing, confirmation, and next-step states are present and truthful.
entries.claim_ceiling: Practitioner completeness reminder; not independent critical-failure authority.
entries.payload: For owned payment flows, check method selection, data entry, validation, processing, success confirmation, and next steps. Reconcile against normative and platform guidance.

use_when: a verified authored world must persist across surfaces
avoid_when: the direction is unverified or surface-local
entries.counterexample: One-off composition values need not become system tokens.
entries.observable_test: Tokens and aliases reproduce validated decisions without claiming that tokenization proves quality.
entries.claim_ceiling: Stable community-group implementation format, not a W3C Recommendation.
entries.payload: After a world earns reuse, serialize primitive, semantic, and component tokens with types, aliases, descriptions, source artifact, exceptions, and validation date.
